detail.longDescription: Using a busybox:1.37 container and its httpd command I am trying to display a react/ts website. I built the container by copying the dist files of my app and adding an httpd.conf containing only 'I:index.html'. I then start it with the command 'busybox httpd -f -vv -h <path_to_dist_files> -c <path_to_httpd.conf> -p <port>' When I request the root url in my browser, everything seems to work properly. For example, I get redirected to <url>/login from <url> if I am not authenticated. BUT when I try to go directly to <url>/login or any other non-root url I get a 404. My app does indeed not have a login directory as a folder, but a Route element from react-router. I thought the httpd.conf direction I:index.html is meant exactly for this case but it did seemingly nothing. I then tried to add E404:index.html to the httpd.conf and that technically worked but I get a 404 error in the console everytime I refresh a non-root page and this seems like an ugly workaround. Am I missing something?
